invariants.rationale: Since screenPos is a Vector3 object that is returned, result should never be null.

Given that screenPos.set(vec.x, vec.y, 0) is always called before the return, result's z component will be set to 0 (or possibly transformed, but generally expected to stay at 0 if isometric transformation preserves the plane).
vec is directly dereferenced (vec.x, vec.y), so it cannot be null at this program point.
Since result is returned as Vector3, this always holds.
